mainEntity.name: Do you provide assisted living & senior living cleaning in Stoughton, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Stoughton (Norfolk County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 28 miles southeast of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Are there assisted living residences in Stoughton?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stoughton's verified healthcare anchor is PAM Health Specialty Hospital of Stoughton (long-term acute care hospital), and practices operate in and around it. We have not verified an individual assisted living residence by name yet; tell us your address and we will confirm scheduling.

mainEntity.name: Which nearby towns do you also serve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The closest served towns to Stoughton are Canton (about 4.1 mi), Sharon (about 4.2 mi), Randolph (about 4.8 mi). See the full list on our service areas page.

mainEntity.name: Do you audit hand hygiene and PPE compliance for us?

acceptedAnswer.text: We audit our own staff, not yours. In the same CDC assessment, 16.8% of the 438 facilities did no observational monitoring of hand hygiene and PPE at all, and assisted living performed worse than nursing homes on several controls — so the gap is real. But monitoring care staff is a residence function tied to your own infection control plan, and a vendor signing off on it would not survive scrutiny. What we provide is our supervisor observation records for cleaning staff, which you can file as part of your program, plus written notice when we observe something in a common area that your team should look at.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle chemicals and carts in a memory care wing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cart is never left unattended in a resident-accessible area — that single practice prevents most incidents. Chemicals travel in labeled secondary containers only, closed, on the lower shelf; concentrates stay in the locked closet and are dispensed there. Doors to housekeeping and soiled utility rooms are closed and secured behind us every time, not propped for convenience. We schedule wet-floor work in memory care during low-traffic windows with signage and a staff member aware, because a wet corridor is a fall risk before it is a cleaning task. Staff are briefed to redirect nothing and call your care team instead.

mainEntity.name: What is explicitly outside your scope in a resident's unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anything that touches the resident or their possessions in a care capacity. We do not provide personal care, assist with transfers, handle personal laundry unless it is a separately contracted linen service, sort or discard belongings, clean inside refrigerators or cupboards without written permission, handle medications or medication carts, or move furniture that a resident relies on for orientation. Clutter that blocks our cleaning gets reported, not resolved by us. Drawing this boundary in the contract protects the residence too: it keeps a cleaning contractor from performing tasks 651 CMR reserves for trained residence staff.

Our sequence, step by step

  1. Enter resident apartments only with permission and at the time agreed.
  2. Escalate cleaning during respiratory or gastrointestinal illness as directed by the residence.
  3. Keep laundry and food-service areas to their own cleaning procedures.
  4. Damp-mop floors with wet-floor signage to reduce fall risk.
  5. Log apartments and common areas completed.

How often

  • Periodic: carpets, windows and high dusting.

Apartment housekeeping days are usually fixed so residents know when to expect the team.

What inspectors cite — and how we prevent it

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Control Assessment and Response (ICAR)

No auditing of hand hygiene and PPE compliance — a written policy exists, but no observational monitoring confirms staff follow it.

16.8% of the same 438 facilities did no such auditing. Assisted living performed materially worse than nursing homes on several controls in that study.

29 CFR 1910.1030 — OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens

Bloodborne pathogens programme deficiencies — exposure control plan, contaminated laundry, regulated waste, surface decontamination and PPE.

Federal OSHA, October 2024 to September 2025: 9 citations across 3 inspections of assisted living facilities, carrying $37,006 in penalties — the largest penalty total of any standard for the sector.

651 CMR 12.04(1)(e) and 651 CMR 12.04(13)(b)1

Failure to meet the State Sanitary Code. This is an express condition of certification for every Massachusetts assisted living residence, and a sponsor must forward any Sanitary Code, Building Code or fire safety citation it receives to the state within seven days.
